title: Detect when orphaned thread is left running
body:
If a user starts a thread from their script, and that thread doesn't have any exit condition, it'll keep running forever. This probably isn't what the user wanted! I don't know that we can detect this in the general case, but maybe we _could_ detect when an orphaned thread is making `st.foo` calls, and show a warning in the terminal.

For example, this user was creating watchdog threads that continue executing after this script completes: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-monitor-the-filesystem-and-have-streamlit-updated-when-some-files-are-modified/822

title: Resolve caching differences in Python 2 vs 3
body:
When hashing a function that returns an object that we can't pickle, python 3 raises a TypeError while python 2 falls back to hashing the name of the non-hashable object.

`get_hash()` therefore raises a TypeError in python 3 but not in python 2.

Evaluate if we can remove the `except` blocks in `_def _code_to_bytes` for python 2 and also handle `None` getting passed to `hasher.update` in `def _update` in hashing.py

title: st.image, st.video, and st.audio should build image, video, and audio headers (respectively) for raw numpy array data
body:
### Problem

Many users want to use Streamlit to programmatically generate images and videos.

Right now we accept numpy arrays as valid data with `st.video` and `st.image`, but we require that the user do the work in their own script of creating the proper headers for those images.  (See streamlit discussion question [Is it possible to embed a tiff/array video with Streamlit?](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/is-it-possible-to-embed-a-tiff-array-video-with-streamlit/1393).

To the extent that is reasonable, we should support automatically creating the appropriate headers for a handful of common formats: JPG, PNG (already expliciltly named), TIFF (as an addition), etc.

Some user research would be useful to see which formats people might benefit from.

### Solution

**MVP:**  (First thought) -- implement another argument in `st.image` and `st.video` like "add_headers" (boolean).

**Possible additions:**  Autodetect the file type based on its contents and add headers appropriately?  This seems like an improbable stretch since filetype detection generally revolves around reading the headers.

**Preferred solution:**  Explicitly support adding headers to specific image and video formats.  TIFF, JPG, PNG, etc.  So the streamlit api would become something like this:

    st.image(image=some_array, format="JPG", add_headers=True)

    st.video(data=some_array, format="TIFF", add_headers=True)

### Additional context

The same should be done for `st.audio` (and there are #todo statements in the code to that effect); this will be opened as a separate issue since the headers for audio wouldn't overlap with image and video headers.

---

title: Play nicer with scripts that spawn children processes
body:
# Summary
When Streamlit interrupts (and terminates) a script that has spawned children processes, the children processes don't appear to be properly handled causing the session to hang and ultimately become unusable. The user must refresh the browser page to continue using the app; the administrator must send SIGKILL signals the streamlit process (and its children) when trying to stop the streamlit server.

# Steps to reproduce
Create a script using `with muiltiprocessing.pool.Pool() as pool:` and submit some tasks to the pool that require some time to finish.
Before the pool has been closed and joined, click Stop or Rerun for the script.
Notice the session is now hung and the children processes that persist.

## Expected behavior:
Streamlit should probably send some king of a signal to the script so it can attempt to terminate itself before Streamlit kills it.

## Actual behavior:
Session is seemingly corrupted and children processes are orphaned.

## Is this a regression?
No

# Debug info
- Streamlit version: 0.53.0
- Python version: 3.8.1
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just a normal virtual environment from python -m venv
- OS version: CentOS Linux 7

# Additional information
[More here discuss.streamlit.io](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/spawning-process-es-within-a-streamlit-script-can-lead-to-a-corrupted-user-session-if-a-script-run-is-interrupted-rerun/1703/2)

title: Make Streamlit easy to deploy as a standalone executable (e.g. PyInstaller, Electron)
body:
Is there a future for electron deployment of streamlit?
___

```
streamlit electron app.py
```

Streamlits target demographic (seemingly the Data Science / ML / AI community) often has apps which consume *a lot* of resources. RAM for loading data used by the app can be quite a bit- pair this with `st.cache` and in a few hours/days time your streamlit app needs to be killed / controlled / scaled. That is fine (and good for AWS' profit), but why not be able to distribute the app across its users so they can run it on their machine (and use their resources).  This is easy enough if your streamlit users are capable of running `streamlit run ..` in their terminal. However, *who are the users of these apps*? Oftentimes they will be other engineers / programmers sure - but I think a substantial chunk of the user-base of streamlit apps is a non-technical audience. We send links to streamlit apps to management / non-technical members of the organization *constantly* I would much rather send them an `S3` link to download an electron app and not worry about scaling up the AWS instance(s) hosting it. Sure, they have to have python and some dependencies - but those are relatively easy to control by IT and can often involve little user work. Furthermore, we could maybe have a future where the `streamlit build electon` command could bundle dependencies? I am not sure - but it seems possible.


Streamlit seems well-positioned for this to be possible. It is trivial to "fake it". Just do something like this to get an *MVP*. 

```python
import streamlit as lit  # you guys really dropped the ball on this not being the suggested import
# idk - maybe it is too z00mer.

def main():
    lit.sidebar.title("Electron")
    lit.sidebar.info("The Electron Slide...")
    lit.sidebar.slider('How "nativive"?', 0, 100, 50)
    lit.title("Streamlit in `Electron`")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Run it,

```
streamlit run app.py
```

Take the starter electron app from [here](https://github.com/electron/electron-quick-start). and change literally 1 line (:16)

```
mainWindow.loadURL('http://localhost:8501/')  // or wherever you served
```

And...

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8339189/79810221-8cb46680-8340-11ea-80a4-8d112f3b4611.png)

___
I am just opening this issue to see if you guys (and the community) think this has any legs. I am not sure of the specifics. For example,

```
streamlit (electron|run_electron) app.py  # for local testing and development
streamlit build -t electron app.py <name>  # for building and bundling dependencies
# to a downloadable launcher? 
...
```

Could there be electron-specific component implementations (so sidebar could be a native window), or tab support, keyboard shortcuts, etc? Could session state be saved to disk and loaded on app start to preserve state? Or maybe this is all a terrible idea... (also if there is another discussion of this already somewhere else (I couldn't find one) lmk and this can just be closed)

---

title: Improve caching of recursive calls
2nd Sidebar (on right side)
body:
### Problem

A neat app often elucidates complex problems. Hence there is often a lot to explain to carry details about the app itself, its backgrounds and further details - especially for public apps. Currently, the little space in the sidebar and main window quickly get filled with explanations and further links. I have written long markdown documents one can hide, but still, either people quickly uncheck the box to head for the box or get overwhelmed with details. Eventually, a good app is not used because of a cluttered layout, long scrolling and still insufficient clarity.

### Solution

**MVP:** A 2nd sidebar on the right side could be a nice designated place for such instructions, background information etc. It would save a lot of real estate in the other sections and still provide novice users with guidance without distracting frequent users. Moreover I consider it rather simple to copy the class from the existing sidebar - just as a right-bound counterpart.

**Possible additions:** Another option cold be an annotation overlay for all controls.

**Preferred solution:** I prefer the simple and straight forward solution

Thanks so much and many cheers.

title: Look for Configuration Files in Platform-Recommended Directories
body:
# Problem

Streamlit uses the home directory for its configuration, but that adds _another_ config file to pollute a home directory. We should be good platform citizens and provide thoughtful locations for configuration files.

# Solution

We as a team agreed on the following order:

1. `$PROJECT_FOLDER/.streamlit`
2. (great if possible, but not required) `$PROJECT_FOLDER/{../}+.streamlit` (i.e. any subfolder containing .streamlit)
3. `~/.config/streamlit` if Unix/macOS (or in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, if defined), `%CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA%/streamlit` if Windows (that's [`ProgramData`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/usmt/usmt-recognized-environment-variables), meaning we follow Git and Conda)
4. `~/.streamlit`

### Additional context

See Closed Pull Request #1907

title: Trigger a script re-run from another thread
body:
I'd love to have some API like `st.request_rerun(user_id: str)` that could be called _outside_ of a user script. (Currently we have `st.experimental_rerun`, but it can only be called by a script that's currently executing).

The use case:

If an app script has some long asynchronous process (for example, uploading a user file to some endpoint that the client does not have access to), there's no good way to signal to Streamlit "please re-run the app for user X" (or: "please re-run the app for all users").

Here's an example from the forums: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-ui-freezes-on-long-api-call/9949

title: Add option to limit st.cache size by memory footprint rather than total number of entries
body:
### Problem

The ability to limit the size of the cache was added by https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/1152 which is extremely useful when deploying a streamlit app to a remote server to prevent a memory leak, however it leaves the question as to what value `max_entries` should be set to.  For example, if my remote server has 1GB of memory and I'd like to allocate 500MB of it for the purposes of caching responses, what values of `max_entries` should I set for each of the functions I am caching to ensure I don't exceed that memory limit?  As of right now the only way to determine it is through trial and error.

### Solution

**MVP:** One solution would be to add another parameter to the `st.cache` function like `max_memory_footprint` to limit the size of the cache by memory rather than number of entries.

**Possible additions:** An addition to this would be a global parameter like `maxCacheSize` in the `config.toml` file, this would be more convenient than limiting memory footprint by function as it may be difficult to determine what the optimal allocation per function would be in the case that you are caching multiple functions. 

**Preferred solution:** The preferred solution would probably be both options, a global memory limit that can be set to prevent the application from running out of memory, and a per-function memory limit for finer control when necessary. 

Thank you!

---

title: Server shutdown fails to exit while processing infinite loop
body:
### Summary

Python process does not exit when shutting down the server while processing an infinite loop in a script

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet: (using a recent SessionState prototype, before I fixed the implementation)

```
import streamlit as st

state = st.get_state()
st.write("printed something")
st.write("foobar" in state) # this line infinite looped before I fixed the implementation
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Run the above snippet against the [previous state prototype](https://github.com/AnOctopus/streamlit/tree/c17d119aef34ae1f15f0e7dff5051469d8bb745d) (I ran the react server as a separate process from the dev install of that commit, rather than running them together via a wheel, don't know if that affects this)
2. C-c in the shell running the python server

**Expected behavior:**

Python server stops, process exits and control returns to my shell

title: Caching improvements
body:
### Problem

I'm using Streamlit to build a complicated report which takes about an hour to generate an output. It processes a hundred megabytes of Pandas dataframes. The performance of this report is important to keep UX better. Data processing has also it's own cost. 

To show report results during a reasonable amount of time and minimize processing costs I utilize caching approach. Using Streamlit's caching mechanism I've faced multiple difficulties:
1. I would like to use persistence on the disk instead of keeping the cache inside in RAM. It helps to avoid wasting RAM when you have multiple nodes where the report is hosted. I understand that it needs time to load the cache into memory but it is excepted. When there are multiple cache values which take 100MB it is reasonable to keep this on disk instead of in RAM to avoid OOM. Unfortunately, Streamlit keeps a copy of cache value in memory when `persist=True`.
2. There are only two strategies of caching: memory and disk. In my particular case, it is reasonable to have the possibility to keep cache directly in S3/Minio.
3. Streamlit has only one strategy of data serialization: Pickle. In the case of large Pandas data frames, it is reasonable to have other formats support like Arrow (it more efficient in term of memory usage and loading time). In general, it would be great to have different strategies which depend on the data type.
4. I'm not able to configure caching folder. Currently, Streamlit keep all cache in `~/.streamlit`

I'm still exploring Streamlit features and code, so probably it is not a complete list of missing cache features.

### Solution

**MVP:**
1. Add `skip_memory_cache=True`
2. As a workaround we can mount S3 into `~/.streamlit` folder using the FUSE driver ([s3 FUSE driver](https://github.com/s3fs-fuse/s3fs-fuse), [Minio FUSE driver](https://github.com/minio/minfs))
3. Pickle is good enough but it does not support unserialization streaming which leads to RAM usage spike.
4. Add cache folder into config (see #3269)
5. Do not remove `cache` directory, because it might be mounted using `s3fs`

**Preferred solution:**
1-2. Add different caching strategies and possibility to chain different strategies (like `cache_strategies=['memory', 'disk', 's3']`). Initially, we can fetch from the fast cache and if it is miss then from the slower cache.
3. Implement data serialization for Pandas. Parquet is a preferable format (see formats [comparison](https://towardsdatascience.com/the-best-format-to-save-pandas-data-414dca023e0d))
4. Cache folder should be a part of `disk` strategy configuration.
5. Decouple cache component as a separate library to avoid coupling on the whole streamlit project. I found this useful when I want to use the same caching approach in my libraries.

### Additional context

Probably integration of an already existing cache library that already supports all these features might be a faster and more robust solution.

Here is a library that can be easily replace FS Python operations with S3:
https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

### Summary

When a widget is redisplayed, the value returned is not the same value the widget shows.

```
import streamlit
```

title: Changing default overrides incoming user selected value
body:
### Summary

As outlined in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/1169#issuecomment-672701734, when a new initial value is passed into a widget, it overwrites any incoming user selected value from the widget - see the example in that comment.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this code snippet and toggle back and forth between the options. After the first click, when a new option is selected the radio will flip back to the previously selected option. This is due to passing in a new default value from the query string.

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

st.title("Experimental: Play with Query Strings!")

app_state = st.experimental_get_query_params()
app_state = {k: v[0] if isinstance(v, list) else v for k, v in app_state.items()} # fetch the first item in each query string as we don't have multiple values for each query string key in this example

# [2] Radio
radio_list = ['Eat', 'Sleep', 'Both']
default_radio = int(app_state["radio"]) if "radio" in app_state else 0

radio = st.radio("What are you doing at home during quarantine?", radio_list, key='what_to_do', index=default_radio)

app_state["radio"] = radio_list.index(radio)
st.experimental_set_query_params(**app_state)

print("")
```

**Expected behavior:**

Expected that the option will respect the users choice first and a changing default second, e.g.; on first load we would pull the defaults from the query string and setup the options accordingly and then as the user changes each one, we update the query string to reflect choices made - perfect for sharing with a colleague!

**Actual behavior:**

When the "state" is pulled out of the URL and passed to the controls, each render, the URL state is "one behind" the user selected value and then is overridden by code which was intended to make sure controls are updated if the default is changed. This was introduced by https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/3477 

### Is this a regression?

I don't think this is a regression - both SessionState and query string parameters are fairly new features.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.84.0
- Python version: 3.8.2
- PyEnv/PipEnv
- OS version: Manjaro/MacOSX
- Browser version: Chromium/Chrome

### Additional information

I discovered this bug while building a feature in an app I was working on where I store the app state in redis, and then put a key=$hash into the query string and noticed that the controls behaved oddly when toggling. I used the workaround in the above linked PR (described by @karriebear) of setting session state variables the first time URL parameters are extracted.

title: Allow initialization of range slider with session state
body:
### Summary

I want to be able to create a slider and a checkbox where if the checkbox is unclicked, the slider functions as normal with some default value `val1`, but if the checkbox is clicked, the slider is locked in to a default value `val2` and resets to this value with every rerun, independent of user action. 

This functionality is possible with a standard slider using session state and key to initialize the slider value depending on the value of the checkbox, however, streamlit throws an error if you attempt to use session state to initialize a tuple of initial values for the slider (i.e. to create a range_slider). 

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:
Functionality for typical single-value slider (this works as expected):
```
import streamlit as st

val1 = 30
val2 = 70
low = 0
high = 100

use_val2 = st.checkbox('Val2?')

if use_val2:
    st.session_state.my_slider = val2
elif 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_slider = val1

slider = st.slider('My slider', min_value=low, max_value=high, key='my_slider')

```

This raises the error:
```
import streamlit as st

val1_0, val1_f = 30, 50
val2_0, val2_f = 70, 90
low = 0
high = 100

use_val2 = st.checkbox('Val2?')

if use_val2:
    st.session_state.my_slider = (val2_0, val2_f)
elif 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_slider = (val1_0, val1_f)

slider = st.slider('My range slider', min_value=low,
                   max_value=high, key='my_slider')

```

**Expected behavior:**

I would like the default slider range to be 30-50 and adjustable if `use_val2` is checked, and 70-90 and fixed if `use_val2` is not checked.

**Actual behavior:**
Raises  `TypeError: (30, 50) has type tuple, but expected one of: int, long, float`

### Is this a regression?

No

title: Selector returns invalid option if present in session_state

If the value of a selector saved in the session_state doesn't match the available options, the selector takes that value anyway even though it's no longer valid.

This can happen if the selector options are dynamic, and interacting with the dashboard changes the options.

title: on_change not called for first session_state value
body:
### Summary

Streamlit 0.84 introduces an [`on_change` callback](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/stable/session_state_api.html#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state) for some interactive widgets as part of the new Session State API. I've found that the callback is not invoked for the first value (i.e., the widget's default or initial value), only for subsequent values.  

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st

def colour_changed():
    st.info(f"colour_changed: {st.session_state.colour}")

colour = st.selectbox("Colour", ["blue", "red", "yellow", "green"], key="colour", on_change=colour_changed)

st.info(f"selectbox returned: {colour}")
```

1. When the report is first run, the selectbox returns `blue` as the selected value, but the `colour_changed()` callback is not called.
2. When a different colour is selected, the selectbox returns the new colour and `colour_changed()` is called.
 
**Expected behavior:**

I believe the `on_change` callback should be called when a widget sets the initial/default value.

I'm finding that the lack of a callback for the initial value greatly complicates things because I can't depend on the callback to do stuff for every value of an interactive widget. I have to write special cases for the initial state.

This is further complicated by what seems like a bug initializing default session_state values for widgets like selectbox (see #3598).

**Actual behavior:**

The `on_change` callback is not called for a widget's initial/default value.

### Is this a regression?

No. The Session State API is new in Streamlit 0.84.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 0.84.2
- Python version: Python 3.8.11
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just pip
- OS version: Debian buster (in a python:3.8 container)
- Browser version: Safari 14.1 on macOS Mojave 10.14.6

### Additional information

None.

title: Exception "The truth value of a Series is ambiguous" when using Pandas row object as widget state
body:
### Summary

Note: this is a new issue when I upgraded streamlit to the current version which added session state.

Suppose I use a pandas object as the selected state for a widget like a radio button (code sample below). Then when changes occur in the widget, an exception is thrown:

```
ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous. Use a.empty, a.bool(), a.item(), a.any() or a.all().
```

### Steps to reproduce
Create a widget like a radio selector where the pandas row object (technically a `pd.Series`) is used as the selected object. Certainly one could use something like an id instead and then look up from the DataFrame, but this used to work and I had code that did things this way. It seemed convenient.

```
selected_object = st.radio("", [o for i, o in df.iterrows()], format_func=lambda o: o["someField"])
```

With the session state update, any selection of a different radio button triggers the exception, because in `session_state.py`, the `_widget_changed` method does a boolean comparison of the selected object. This isn't allowed with `pd.Series` objects.

```
    def _widget_changed(self, widget_id: str) -> bool:
        new_value = self._new_widget_state.get(widget_id)
        old_value = self._old_state.get(widget_id)
        changed: bool = new_value != old_value
        return changed
```

**Expected behavior:**

Support pd.Series objects as widget selected values.

**Actual behavior:**

Exception is thrown, application fails to function.

### Is this a regression?

Yes, worked before session state was added.

### Debug info

Seen in streamlit 0.86.0

### Summary
Ghost elements appear in the sidebar on app reruns; in particular after ticking and unticking checkboxes in the sidebar. This behaviour started in versions >0.83 (i.e after Session State was introduced)

The attached screencasts show a toy app illustrating the bug introduced after V0.83. Ticking and unticking checkboxes in the sidebar results in ghost headers haunting the screen. The ‘ghosts’ are mainly headers in the sidebar but sometimes ghost widgets also haunt the sidebar. The toy app includes a checkbox on the main page. title: Session state setting failing to propagate to frontend
body:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/problems-with-the-new-widget-behaviour-under-streamlit-0-89-0/17625

I investigated using the script from the post. The value seen in session state itself is being set correctly, but `should_set_frontend_state_value` incorrectly returns False. It seems like the check for `is_new_widget_value` shouldn't be part of that method. The method implementation should have been a conservative simplification of the old one that stripped out the initial value handling and separated this check from setting the value of a new widget, so I can't see why the script would have worked in 0.88, but also the current behavior is obviously incorrect.

Removing the second part of the check would make it match the obvious notion that the frontend should have its value overridden whenever the value is set in session state, and trying out this change locally appears to fix the problem.

title: Setting widget values using session_state does not work after initialization
body:
### Summary

If a widget's value is set by modifying the session state the widget does not update.

The [docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state) state

> We can set and get the value of the temperature widget by using the Session State API

### Steps to reproduce

If you take the example stated in the docs that works fine and sets the value, but only for the first run

```
import streamlit as st

if "celsius" not in st.session_state:
    # set the initial default value of the slider widget
    st.session_state.celsius = 50.0

st.slider(
    "Temperature in Celsius",
    min_value=-100.0,
    max_value=100.0,
    key="celsius"
)

# This will get the value of the slider widget
st.write(st.session_state.celsius)
```
If you modify the session state before the widget is "initialized" the GUI does not update,
but the actual value returned from the widget is the one set.

e.g. with the following example:

```
import streamlit as st
import datetime

def cbk_text_input():
    st.write('callback text')
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

def cbk_slider():
    st.write('callback slider')
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

if 'id_input' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['id_input'] = ''

if 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['my_slider'] = 5

# these values do not reflect in the GUI,
# but they do in the actual value returned from the widget
st.session_state['id_input'] = 'sdf'
st.session_state['my_slider'] = 50

answer = st.text_input(f'', value='', 
                            key='id_input',
                            on_change=cbk_text_input)

x = st.slider('some slider', key='my_slider',
                         min_value=0,
                         max_value=100,
                         value=4,
                         step=5,
                         on_change=cbk_slider)

answer
st.session_state['id_input']
x
st.session_state['my_slider']
```
But I would expect the widget to also reflect a "manual" change to the session state.
I would have expected the slider to move and the text box to change its content.

### Is this a regression?

no clue

body:
### Summary

When using State API st.number_input() always result in a warning: `The widget with key "...." was created with a default value but also had its value set via the Session State API.`

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
st.session_state['comp.pagination.chunk_size'] = 5
items_per_page = component.number_input(
        "Genes per page:",
        min_value=1,
        max_value=100,
        key='comp.pagination.chunk_size'
)


```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Go ceate a simple app with number_input comp
2. Run `streamlit run app.py`
3. You will see a waring

**Expected behavior:**

Expected: No warning

**Actual behavior:**

Actual: Warning is shown.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/72933/137596977-4758e2ad-dcf0-444e-bf48-2dbf8235839c.png)


### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.00.
- Python version: 3.8.1
- Using Conda
- OS version: MacOS 11.3
- Browser version: Safari

### Additional information

The issue is because `NumberInputMixin.number_input` initializes `value` with not None default:
```
class NumberInputMixin:
    def number_input(
        self,
        label: str,
        min_value: Optional[Number] = None,
        max_value: Optional[Number] = None,
        value=NoValue(),
        ...
```

so the check doesn't work properly, because it assumes that not initialized state corresponds to `None`
```
check_session_state_rules(default_value=value, key=key)
```
Here I cannot pass `value=None` as a workaround because `NumberInputMixin` because then I'll get `All numerical arguments must be of the same type`. 

So expected behaviour is to init `value` with `None`. Then if key exists in state update it from state, otherwise show warning that widget already initialized from session API.

title: Widget use of `index` and `key` together... `index` overrides `key`
body:
### Summary

Since the refactoring of widgets in v.0.89, I've had some issues setting the default widget values. I can use `index` and `value` to do this, but that creates conflict with other dynamic rendering I've put in place

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
st.sidebar.radio('Radio', options=[True, False], key='stype')

if st.session_state['stype'] == True:
    st.write("do something")
else:
    st.write("do something else")
```

That works fine. But let's say I have multiple menus on the sidebar...

```
st.sidebar.selectbox('Select', options=['Menu1', 'Menu2'], key='mtype')

if st.session_state.mtype == 'Menu1':
    st.sidebar.radio('Radio', options=[True, False], key='stype')
    
    if st.session_state['stype'] == True:
        st.write("do something")
    else:
        st.write("do something else")
else:
    st.write("second menu")
```
This code kind of works. I can set the session_states `stype` and `mtype`, but when I switch between Menu1 and Menu2, Menu 1 widgets get erased from the page. Still ok. `st.session_state['stype']` is set as expected (to the value set by the widget). However, let's say I set the Radio widget to `False`, when I switch back to Menu1 (from Menu2), a new Radio widget is created with a default value (e.g. `index=0`).

**This updates the session state** to `st.session_state['stype'] = True`

Supposedly I can use `index` to set the default behavior of the widget like:

```
st.sidebar.radio('Radio', options=[True, False], index=0, key='stype')
```
but what I really want is a dynamic index, that adjusts to the session_state previously set, like
```
st.sidebar.radio('Radio', options=[True, False], index=[True, False].index(st.session_state['stype']), key='stype')
```

title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
body:
### Problem

Right now streamlit requires a raw Python script (e.g. `your_script.py`) that is invoked, e.g.
```
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]
```

This is really frustrating if you want to package your streamlit application in a wheel file and distribute it to your friends & colleagues.  Streamlit's requirement of a raw Python script makes this impossible.

Assume I have created a proper Python package/distribution `my-streamlit-dashboard` and uploaded it to PyPI or some company-internal artefact store. If my colleagues now runs `pip install my-streamlit-dashboard`, my package will be installed but how would my colleague now run my dashboard? There is no `script.py` entry point for him or her to run. 


### Solution

For use-cases like this, Python packaging allows the definition of `console_scripts` which allow you to define command-line scripts that are installed e.g. within your virtual environment, and behave like normal shell scripts (but are actual Python scripts). All details can be found [here](https://python-packaging.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command-line-scripts.html#the-console-scripts-entry-point). Quite many Python tools & frameworks use this capability like for instance [PyScaffold's `putup` command](https://github.com/pyscaffold/pyscaffold), [Django's `django-admin` command](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.2/ref/django-admin/), [poetry's `poetry` command](https://python-poetry.org/docs/) and streamlit's own `streamlit` command.

Continuing the example from above, I could define a console-script `my-cool-dashboard` within the package `my-streamlit-dashboard` that would act as the initial script to run for streamlit, i.e.
```
streamlit run my-streamlit-dashboard
```
For this to work, streamlit would need to allow console scripts defined by `console_scripts` as start points for dashboard. Technically this should be possible as they are just Python scripts. Doing this right now leads to the error:
```
Error: Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.
For more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io
```
if the console script doesn't end with `.py`, which is common. Adding `.py` leads to:
```
Error: Invalid value: File does not exist: my-cool-dashboard.py
```
A crude and unsatisfying workaround is:
```
streamlit run `which my-cool-dashboard.py`
```
This seems to mostly work but also emits nasty errors during execution:
```
File "/Users/fwilhelm/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 354, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/Users/fwilhelm/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/bin/my-streamlit-dashboard.py", line 33, in <module>
    sys.exit(load_entry_point('my-streamlit-dashboard', 'console_scripts', 'my-cool-dashboard.py')())
```


### Additional context

What are the benefits of making packaging for streamlit apps possible? I'm glad you asked! 
* Another way of distribution. For production, a streamlit app would right now be deployed as docker container most likely. Allowing proper packaging would also make it possible for users to just install and run it locally via pip. Thus more **flexibility**.
* Proper **versioning**. Since Python packages/distributions are versioned, one could apply proper versioning to these packages and enforce certain processes within an organisation, like semantic versioning etc. which is hard if everyone is just cloning a git repo. 
* Enabling [**ML-Ops** principles](https://ml-ops.org/content/mlops-principles). Most organisation provide templates for Python projects that support developers in applying techniques like testing (CI/CD), reproducibility, documentation, deployment, etc. With the suggested solution it would be much easier to incorporate streamlit in such templates as e.g. provided by [PyScaffold](https://pyscaffold.org/).

---

title: st.experimental_get_query_params() does not work with Always Rerun
body:
### Summary

When using st.experimental_get_query_params() and Always Rerun on source code changes, the query params will return an empty dict after a couple of code changes. This is frustrating for any app that uses query params because you can't just turn on Always Rerun or your app breaks after a couple code changes. 

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

st.text('1')
st.write(st.experimental_get_query_params())
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Open your browser to the URL with some query params like http://localhost:8501?param=something
3. Edit the '1' to a '2'
4. In browser pre 'r' for rerun. 
5. The query params should be correct. Rerun seems to work fine. 
6. Now edit the '2' to a '3' in the code. 
7. This time press 'a' to always rerun. 
8. The first time the query params should be correct. 
9. Edit '3' to '4'. 
10. The query params will now come back as an empty dict `{}`

**Expected behavior:**

The query params should not change, the URL in the browser is still there an correct with `param=something`

**Actual behavior:**

An empty dict is returned. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2138258/148153409-c67198dd-d58c-4b94-b5c4-919c5674fe1e.png)


### Is this a regression?

Not sure if this ever worked. 

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.3.1
- Python version: 3.7.6
- Using virtualenv
- OS version: 10.15.7
- Browser version: Chrome 96.0.4664.110

### Additional information

I did some printing in the codebase and a fix is to replace: 
```
client_state.query_string = self._client_state.query_string
```
with:
```
 client_state.query_string = self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string
```
here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L184
to look like: 
```
    client_state = ClientState()
    client_state.query_string = self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string
    widget_states = self._session_state.as_widget_states()
    client_state.widget_states.widgets.extend(widget_states)
    self.on_event.send(ScriptRunnerEvent.SHUTDOWN, client_state=client_state)
```
otherwise the self._client_state seems to never be set in the first place with the query string. If you print out `self._client_state.query_string` versus `self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string` you'll see that the former is empty upon the first run whereas the latter is filled with the query params after the first run. The reason is the ctx is set here https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L273 but the self._client_state is not. 

The SHUTDOWN signal triggered by `self.on_event.send`, therefore, sets into the ReportSession the empty query string to the ReportSession's self._client_state [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/report_session.py#L354) which is then used to create the ScriptRunner in the next rerun when a file changes [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/report_session.py#L575).  

It seems better to use the `self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx` value as well because `experimental_set_query_params()` can set the query_string in the ctx during script running, so the self._client_state is also incorrect in that scenario. The proposed fix seems to correct both issues of Always Run not working and `experimental_set_query_params()` being not passing it's query_string back to the ReportSession either. 

I don't believe the widget_states in the ClientState proto have the same issue because they are being set on each script run [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L349) as the self._session_state which is used to fill in the ClientState returned from ScriptRunner on shutdown.

Setting widget default values through session_state works. However, a momentary interruption (`st.stop()`) between the initialization of the session state and the initialization of the widget generates a bug in the appearance of widgets.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import streamlit as st

if "celsius" not in st.session_state:
    # set the initial default value of the slider widget
    st.session_state.celsius = 50.0

st.session_state["stop"] = st.selectbox(label="Select 'no'", options=["yes", "no"])
if st.session_state["stop"] == "yes":
    st.stop()

slider_value = st.slider(
    "Temperature in Celsius",
    min_value=-100.0,
    max_value=100.0,
    key="celsius"
)
st.write(f"session state: {st.session_state.celsius}")
st.write(f"value of widget: {slider_value}")
st.write("That's weird: visually, the slider is set to -100!")
```

Note that the problem does not appear if `st.stop()` is put at the beginning of the code.

title: Non-invertible `format_func` breaks widget serialization/caching
body:
### Summary

An app with an input widget whose options can take different sets of values (e.g. select box with `["Alice", "Bob"]` and `["Amy", "Barry"]` as below) seems to cache the widget state based only on the `format_func`'ed option values, rather than the raw values.   In example below, the app initially serializes the select box `Selectbox(["Alice", "Bob"])` as `Selectbox(["A", "B"])`. When the select box changes to `Selectbox(["Amy", "Barry"])`, it is still serialized as `Selectbox(["A", "B"])`, leading to streamlit trying to find `"Amy"` in the cached `Selectbox(["Alice", "Bob"])`, thus resulting in the observed `ValueError`.

title: Inconsistent session state behavior when used with widgets
body:
### Summary

Session state in Streamlit 0.89.0 to 1.5.0 has a strange behavior when bound to widgets (`key` parameter).

### Steps to reproduce

#### First case

1. In the same script run, initialize a session state item, and display a widget bound to it.
2. Make the widget disappear (by unchecking a checkbox for instance).
3. Reload with `R`. **ISSUE: Session state item doesn't exist anymore.**
4. Reload again multiple times. **ISSUE: Session state is cleared every other run.**

#### Second case

1. In a first script run, initialize a session state item.
2. In a second run, display a widget bound to the previous session state item (by checking a checkbox for instance).  
    **ISSUE: Widget does not take value from session state.**
3. Change widget value, it updates the session state item correctly.
4. Make the widget disappear.
5. Reload with `R`. **ISSUE: Session state item resets to its initial value**.

#### Code snippet

Feel free to compare the following script behavior with Streamlit 0.88.0 (working session state) and Streamlit 1.5.0. Both cases are implemented.

```python
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

c1, c2 = st.columns(2)

with c1:
    st.subheader("Widget session state item 1")
    st.write("Session state and widget setup in the same run.")
    st.write("When widget disappear, session state item is cleared every other run.")

    with st.echo(code_location="below"):
        if "widget_bound" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.widget_bound = "hello"
            st.success(f"Item added: {st.session_state.widget_bound}")
        else:
            st.info(f"Item exists already: {st.session_state.widget_bound}")

        # Displayed from the beginning by default
        if st.checkbox("Display widget", True):
            st.text_input("Some widget", key="widget_bound")

with c2:
    st.subheader("Widget session state item 2")
    st.write("Session state setup first, then widget in another run.")
    st.write("Widget does not get value initial value from session state.")

    with st.echo(code_location="below"):
        if "widget_unbound" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.widget_unbound = "hello"
            st.success(f"Item added: {st.session_state.widget_unbound}")
        else:
            st.info(f"Item exists already: {st.session_state.widget_unbound}")

        # Displayed after session state initialization
        if st.checkbox("Display widget", False):
            st.text_input("Some widget", key="widget_unbound")
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes, session state with widgets worked as expected from version 0.86.0 to 0.88.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.89.0 to 1.5.0
- Python version: 3.8.6 (pyenv)

title: Query parameters are not read on first run in streamlit cloud
body:
### Summary

When deploying an app to streamlit cloud, I discovered that query parameters behaved differently than in my local development version. In my app, I set a default value for a field in `session_state` if it is not provided through query parameters, but I could never get the query parameters to work on the cloud deployment. After some debugging, I found that query parameters always seem to be empty on the first run of the app in streamlit cloud.
 
### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import logging

import streamlit as st

params = st.experimental_get_query_params()
logging.info(f"{params=}")
if "my-field" not in params:
    st.session_state["MY_FIELD"] = "some default value"

params_second = st.experimental_get_query_params()
if "MY_FIELD" in st.session_state:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=} {st.session_state['MY_FIELD']=}")
else:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=}")

st.write(params)
```
Open app in browser with query parameter like this `?my-field=0`

**Localhost behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:47:46.902 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:47:46.903 params_second={'my-field': ['0']}
```

**Streamlit cloud behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params_second={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params_second={'my-field': ['0']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
```

You can see that the app seems to run twice on streamlit cloud. In the first run the query parameters are empty (except a `timestamp`). The default value will get set in the session_state. In the second run the query parameters are present but the default value has already been set.

### Is this a regression?

I don't know.

### Debug info

- Streamlit, version 1.4.0
- Python 3.9.10
- Browser version: Chrome Version 97.0.4692.99

title: Enable `request_rerun`-ing session through external sources and using a session_id
body:
_(Note, you don't have to fill out every section here. They're just here for guidance. That said, nicely detailed feature requests are more likely to get eng attention sooner)_

### Problem

Dear StreamLit Team, first of all, thank you deeply for this awesome framework. I have learned quite a lot diving through the codebase and resolved some long lasting issues of mine thanks to your ScriptRunner magic :)

I have been playing with StreamLit recently and I have the need to refresh a user tab from an external source, ideally from external requests.

I couldn't find the recommended way to do it, so I hacked StreamLit internals. 

I found an almost unused Handler (DebugHandler) on the tornado routes and patched it to enable receiving a refresh from outside using its get method.

```py
...
if _STREAMLIT_AVAILABLE:
    import urllib.parse as _parse

    import streamlit as st
    import streamlit.bootstrap as bootstrap
    import tornado
    from streamlit import config
    from streamlit.bootstrap import (
        _fix_matplotlib_crash,
        _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning,
        _fix_sys_argv,
        _fix_sys_path,
        _fix_tornado_crash,
        _install_config_watchers,
        _on_server_start,
        _set_up_signal_handler,
    )
    from streamlit.cli import _get_command_line_as_string, check_credentials
    from streamlit.report_thread import get_report_ctx
    from streamlit.server.server import Server
    from tornado.web import RequestHandler

    class RefreshSessionHandler(RequestHandler):
        def initialize(self, server):
            self._server = server

        async def get(self):
            query_arguments = self.request.query_arguments
            session_info = ast.literal_eval([v for v in query_arguments.keys()][0])
            session_id = session_info["session_id"]
            session_info = Server.get_current()._get_session_info(session_id)
            if session_info is None:
                return
            session = session_info.session

            session.request_rerun(session._client_state)

    st.server.server.DebugHandler = RefreshSessionHandler


def _render_ui(script_path, args=None, **flag_options):
    # This code has been taken from StreamLit, so we can patch the DebugHandler
    # with our RefreshSessionHandler
    bootstrap.load_config_options(flag_options=flag_options)

    if args is None:
        args = []

    if flag_options is None:
        flag_options = {}

    command_line = _get_command_line_as_string()

    st._is_running_with_streamlit = True
    check_credentials()
    _fix_sys_path(script_path)
    _fix_matplotlib_crash()
    _fix_tornado_crash()
    _fix_sys_argv(script_path, args)
    _fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning()
    _install_config_watchers(flag_options)
    _set_up_signal_handler()
    ioloop = tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.current()
    with mock.patch("streamlit.server.server.DebugHandler", RefreshSessionHandler):
        server = Server(ioloop, script_path, command_line)
    server.start(_on_server_start)
    server.add_preheated_report_session()
    ioloop.start()
```

This worked perfectly for StreamLit 1.3.9, but the API has changed quite a lot since then and this hack doesn't work.

However, I believe there would be a growing community need to have a more reliable way for external sources to refresh a StreamLit UI. I believe this would be worth prioritizing.

As a side note, I have been investigating how to unittest StreamLit UI behaviour and looked into this test [test_calls_widget_callbacks](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/tests/streamlit/scriptrunner/script_runner_test.py#L142) in particular.

I have used the `TestScriptRunner` to test my StreamLit apps, but its API changed between versions. I would like to ask the StreamLit Team to invest in making the testing tool stable and part of the main package. This would become critical for users to reliability productionize StreamLit apps.
And I am afraid this would create friction to buy into the StreamLit ecosystem if this isn't made available by the Core Team.

Thanks for you deeply for your time and effort !

---

title: An option to keep component values in the session state
body:
### Problem

Component values are automatically saved into the session state, but they are removed if they do not appear in the next run.
However, I sometimes want the component values to be kept in the session state if they appear at least once in some run.

For example, with the code below,
```python
import streamlit as st

page = st.radio("Page", ["page1", "page2"])

if page == "page1":
    st.text_input("Text1", key="text1")
elif page == "page2":
    st.text_input("Text2", key="text2")
```
1. The "page1" is selected on the radio at first.
2. The user inputs some text in the "Text1" text input.
3. The user changes the page to "page2".
4. The user changes the page back to "page1".
5. Then, the "Text1" text input became empty, and the corresponding field in the session state has been removed. I want it to be kept as the value input at 2.


I think this feature is demanded, for example, with multi-page apps.

### Solution

**MVP:** Some new option like `keep_value` is added to all the input components.

body:
### Summary

I created two sliders with default range values. Slider X uses the "sessionstate" pattern (only setting "key"); Slider Y uses both "value" and "key" (without explicitly setting "sessionstate"). The first slider loses its range value when it is clicked and becomes a single value.

### Steps to reproduce

```
import streamlit as st
if "x" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["x"] = (3,7)
x = st.slider("x", min_value=0, max_value=10, key="x")
y = st.slider("y", min_value=0, max_value=10, value=(2,8), key="y")
st.write(st.session_state)
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Go to the main page.
2. Click on any of the sliders.
3. Click on the "x" slider (both left and right ends).

**Expected behavior:**

Expected "x" slider to maintain a range value [a, b] like "y" slider.

title: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
body:
### Problem

I wanted to create a Streamlit application which has an input text field which immediately responds to user input, e.g. like the Google search field does. Something like this:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_input=search_callback)
```

### Solution

I couldn't find any way to achieve this with Streamlit. I think what would be necessary is a new type of `on_input` callback or similar.

Further, I think it would make sense to have a kwarg containing the current input. I would also have liked this for the `on_change` callback. As a workaround I have been using the session state instead:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_change=search_callback)
```

body:
### Summary

Plotly 3D animations normally allow user interactions (zoom, rotating figure with the mouse) to persist across frames.
Some animations (e.g. go.Mesh3d with frames) reset the camera despite the Streamlit user changing its params.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4653)

![dXQum](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/70368164/165344941-fc4cd84e-5a1a-4bae-bccf-d1f22af7ef9a.gif)

This animation displays frames containing each 32 go.Mesh3d() traces (one per facet of the soccer ball).

Steps (see GIF above):

1. interact with the figure (zoom and/or rotating it with the mouse)
2. either click the Plotly figure button 'Play' or move the slider with the mouse
3. watch the figure camera reset itself unwantedly

Can provide MRE if needed.

**Expected behavior:**

The camera position changed by the user persists across frames.

**Actual behavior:**

The camera position changed by the user gets reset to its initial value. Even using [`uirevision`](https://plotly.com/python/reference/layout/#layout-uirevision)


### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.8.1
- Python version: 3.10.0
- OS version: Ubuntu 20.04 (WSL2)
- Browser version: Chrome 100

### Additional information

This issue has been mentioned in a number of threads on SO and plotly Community, see e.g. [here](https://community.plotly.com/t/preserving-ui-state-like-zoom-in-dcc-graph-with-uirevision-with-dash/15793) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58345327/prevent-camera-resetting-after-plotting-with-plotly-python). It is suggested [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-keep-the-view-of-a-plotly-plot-when-changing-a-parameter/2952) in the Streamlit forum that using session state might do the trick, but I couldn't make it work.
Last, I have noticed that commenting out `layout="wide"` from `st.set_page_config` avoids this bug but only between the Streamlit session start and the first interaction with a Streamlit widget

title: Using multiprocessing module
body:
### Problem

I have some CPU-bound tasks and want to use `multiprocessing` module.

But, `multiprocessing` module can only used in `if __name__ == "__main__"` or with in a function.

For example, a flask app:

```python
from multiprocessing import Pool
import time
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

def expensive_function(x):
    time.sleep(4)
    return x*x


@app.route('/')
def expcalc():
    t = time.time()
    with Pool() as p:
        f = p.map(expensive_function, range(4))
    return f'time: {time.time() -t }, Result is'+str(f)

if __name__=='__main__':
    app.run()

```
Either `python app.py` or `gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 app:app` is okey.

BUT, if I do it in streamlit:

```python
from time import sleep, time
import streamlit as st
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed, ProcessPoolExecutor
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

st.title("parallel")

def slow_process(width:int):
    sleep(3)
    return pd.DataFrame(np.random.rand(3,width))


input_args = [3,5,7,9]

t1 = time()
flist = []

if __name__ == "__main__":

    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as executor:
        for arg in input_args:
            flist.append(executor.submit(slow_process, arg))

    for f in flist:
        rdf = f.result()
        st.dataframe(rdf)

    st.write(f"total time usage: {time() - t1}s")
```
I only got  several warnings:

```
2022-05-27 16:58:54.860 WARNING root: 
  Warning: to view a Streamlit app on a browser, use Streamlit in a file and
  run it with the following command:

    streamlit run [FILE_NAME] [ARGUMENTS]
```

What's the right way to use `multiprocessing` module?

title: Session State to Prepopulate Inputs
body:
### Summary

I have a multipage app and I am trying to prepopulate the inputs on Page 1 with their previous input (if it exists) using st.session_state. The code I have written seemingly works at first (prepopulates the default value with their previous input) but when you go to change the value of the input, it seemingly deletes your entry and forces you to re-enter the value (works on the second attempt).  I have tested this on text_input and multiselect but I imagine this happens with other inputs as well.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st   #1.6.0

def load_previous_input(label):
    """If it exists, populate input with previous user entry, otherwise None"""
    return st.session_state[label] if label in st.session_state else None

def save_input(label, new_value):
    """Overwrite previous input with new input"""
    st.session_state[label] = new_value

with st.sidebar:
    selected_page = st.radio('Select Page', ['Page 1', 'Page 2'])

if selected_page == 'Page 1':
    label = 'Enter Some Text'
    value = load_previous_input(label)
    user_text = st.text_input(label, value) if value is not None else st.text_input(label)
    save_input(label, user_text)

elif selected_page == 'Page 2':
    st.write("""Page 2: User does stuff on this page, when clicking back to Page 1, I want the field to
    prepopulate with what they entered before (if it exists). It seemingly works, (prepopulates with previous input)
    but look what happens when you try to change the text...
    """)
```

**Expected behavior:**

I expect to be able to change the value of the input without it getting erased and having to re-enter it a second time for it to stay.

**Actual behavior:**

First entry when trying to change the value is immediately erased, have to type input in a second time for it to stick.

### Is this a regression?

Never attempted this before on previous versions.

### Steps to reproduce

```
import streamlit as st
```

```
# multiselect that works

    st.multiselect("Will keep values when hidden and redisplayed", list(range(100)), key="key1")
```

title: widget state not synced between multiple pages
body:
### Summary

I noticed that the widget state for inputs with same keys is not synced when switching pages.
This comes a bit surprising with the [documented](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/get-started/multipage-apps#notes) and observed  shared session state.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4989)

Code snippet:

- index.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.session_state)
```
- pages/a.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```
- pages/b.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```

(Please provide a code snippet! This will help expedite us finding and solving the problem.)

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Run `streamlit run index.py`
2. Click on Page A
3. Enter text into input
4. Click on Page B
5. See preserved session state, but empty input widget

**Expected behavior:**

Widgets with same user keys should be synced when switching pages.

**Actual behavior:**

Widget state goes out-of-sync with session state.

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.11.0
- Python version: 3.10.0
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Nope
- OS version: Fedora 36
- Browser version: Brave/Chrome

### Additional information

Current **workaround** is to explicitly copy over the previous' page widget state into the session state to populate widgets using the same keys.
```py
st.session_state.update(st.session_state)
```

To not force widgets to invalid selections, our actually used workaround only does so on page navigation.

```py
if ctx := get_script_run_ctx():
    new_page = ctx.page_script_hash
else:
    logger.warning('Missing streamlit context')
    new_page = 'unknown'

old_page = st.session_state.get('_page_script_hash')

if new_page != old_page:
    # https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4989
    st.session_state.update(st.session_state)

st.session_state['_page_script_hash'] = new_page
```

Also see:
- [Session State and Widget State association](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#session-state-and-widget-state-association)
- [An option to keep component values in the session state · Issue #4458 · streamlit/streamlit](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4458)
- [Preserve widget state when a widget disappears from the page (demoed via Multipage Apps) · Issue #5813](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5813).

title: Inconsistent behavior when value is outside of (min_value, max_value) for st.slider and st.number_value
body:
### Summary

st.slider and st.number_input handles 'value' outside of the interval defined by ('min_value', 'max_value') differently. st.slider expands the interval such that 'value' is included in the interval, f.ex. if 'min_value' is 1, 'max_value' is 10 and 'value' is 12, then the slider has the interval (1, 12) instead of (1, 10). st.number_input on the other hand throws and exception when 'value' is outside of the interval ('min_value', 'max_value').

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5099)

```
import streamlit as st

age = st.slider('How old are you?', min_value=1, max_value=10, value=12)
st.write("I'm ", age, 'years old')

age = st.number_input('How old are you?', min_value=1, max_value=10, value=12)
st.write("I'm ", age, 'years old')
```


**Expected behavior:**

I would expect that either both the slider and number_input throws an exception or that both expands the accepted interval values can be in.

**Actual behavior:**

The slider expands the interval to (1, 12) while the number_input throws and exception.

### Is this a regression?

I'm not sure. I'm just starting to use Streamlit, but I checked version 1.3, 1.5 and 1.11 and all had the same behaviour.

title: Pass state as parameter to `on_change` callback
body:
### Problem

Currently it seems you need to access `st.session_state` to figure out what value was selected in the `on_change` callback, but that's limiting if you'd like to create more generic functions to handle these things.

### Solution

Send the selected value (and potentially index) automatically to the `on_change` callback function.

### Additional context

This would allow doing something like:

```python
def update_params(**kwargs):
    st.experimental_set_query_params({kwargs["param_name"]: kwargs["selected_value"]})

    "Select something:",
   ["Select....", "cat", "dog"],
    key="selection_1",
    # value and id get sent automatically as kwargs!
    on_change=update_params,
    kwargs={"param_name": "selection_1"},
)
```

Which is slightly nicer IMHO than having a function for every selectbox.

Let me know if this isn't clear or doesn't make sense though...

title: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" when using st.cache_data in thread
body: ### Summary If fetching data from multiple sources, it can be tempting to run code concurrently as well as cache the results. However, this causes problems when using st.experimental_memo. It results in the error: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" ### Steps to reproduce [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5402) The following code should show it quite clearly: ```python import logging import time import threading import streamlit as st from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import add_script_run_ctx @st.experimental_memo(ttl=1) def function1(interval): interval = interval/4 logging.info("sleeping for %s seconds", interval) time.sleep(interval) logging.info("done sleeping for %s seconds", interval) return interval def main(): format = "%(asctime)s: %(message)s" logging.basicConfig(format=format) threads = [] for index in range(25): x = threading.Thread(target=function1, args=(index,)) # Hack to remove the following logging messages: # `Thread 'Thread-123': missing ScriptRunContext` # see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1326 add_script_run_ctx(x) threads.append(x) x.start() logging.info("Waiting for threads to finish") for thread in threads: thread.join() logging.info("done") st.write("done") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` **Expected behavior:** The threaded function should be run. No error should be shown. **Actual behavior:** The function runs fine. The data is cached. But, the frontend fails with an ugly error message: "Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])" ### Is this a regression? I don't think so ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.12.2 - Python version: 3.9.13 - Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Poetry - OS version: Mac OSx 12.2.1 - Browser version: Chrome 104.0.5112.101 ### Additional information This appears to be caused by st.experimental_memo defaulting to showing a spinner while it's running. If you change line 8 to: `@st.experimental_memo(ttl=1, show_spinner=False)` the error does not happen.

title: Reset widget state by deleting the session state value
body:
### Summary

Deleting the key of a selectbox widget from the session only leads to a half reset of it. The output variable is reset to the default, but the actual widget display is stuck on the previous selection.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5442)

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

selected_option = st.selectbox('Option', ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'], key = 'selection_box')
st.write(f"Selected option: {selected_option }")

if st.button('Reset selection'):
    del st.session_state['selection_box']
    st.experimental_rerun()
```
Select an option other than A, confirm that it is printed out below. "Reset" the widget with pressing the button.

**Expected behavior:**

That the selection widget goes back to selecting option A and prints that as the "selected_option" variable.

**Actual behavior:**

The selectbox is still stuck on the previous selection but the variable "selected_option" has been updated back to the default giving a missmatch between widget state and widget output.

With pressing rerun the variable "selected_option" get's set again to the previously selected option so that the widget state and output are identical, but it will never fully be reset to the default option.

title: Directly provide form submission data to form submit callback
body:
### Summary

The use of callbacks with forms requires a lot of extra boilerplate code to retrieve the values from the session state within the callback function. The workflow is not really generic and makes the usage of callbacks less favourable.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5498)

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st


def test_1(val_1, val_2):

    st.write(f"val_1: {val_1}")
    st.write("----------------")
    st.write(f"val_2: {val_2}")
    st.write("----------------")

    # This could be a CRUD function


def test_2(val_1_key, val_2_key):

    st.write(f"val_1_key: {st.session_state[val_1_key] if val_1_key in st.session_state else 'Key-Error'}")
    st.write("----------------")
    st.write(f"val_2_key: {st.session_state[val_2_key] if val_2_key in st.session_state else 'Key-Error'}")
    st.write("----------------")

    # This could be a CRUD function


def insert_database(id: int, text: str) -> None:

    with st.spinner(text="Writing to database"):

        st.write(id)
        st.write(text)


def prepare_insert_database(id: int, key_identifier: str):

    # This middleware function is not really generic... Probably there are variation which value is in the session_state and which is fixed
    insert_database(id=id, text=st.session_state[key_identifier])


def main():

    with st.expander("Example without forms"):

        st.text_area(label="Please enter values", key="text_refs")

        st.button(label="Submit", on_click=test_1, kwargs=dict(val_1=10, val_2=st.session_state.text_refs))

        st.session_state["submit_v2_val1"] = 10

        st.button(label="Submit - V2", on_click=test_2, kwargs=dict(val_1_key="submit_v2_val1", val_2_key="text_refs"))

    with st.expander("With forms"):

        with st.form(key="form_master_key", clear_on_submit=True):

            st.text_area(label="Please enter values", key="text_refs_form")

            test_val = 11
            st.session_state["submit_v2_val1_form"] = test_val

            # This doesn't work and the displayed value is one behind.
            st.form_submit_button(label="Submit with on-click-Event", on_click=test_1, kwargs=dict(val_1=10, val_2=st.session_state.text_refs_form))

            # This works but submitting keys to function to retrieve the real values within the function. This feels not really pythonic
            # st.form_submit_button(label="Submit with on-click-Event and keys", on_click=test_2, kwargs=dict(val_1_key="submit_v2_val1_form", val_2_key="text_refs_form"))

    # Start examples

    st.header("Real-Example without Callback and Form")

    input_reference = st.text_input("Please input text", key="real_example_no_callback_reference")

    if st.button("Save data"):

        insert_database(id=0, text=input_reference)

    st.header("Real-Example with Callback and Form (Working)")

    with st.form(key="real_example_form", clear_on_submit=True):

        input_reference_2 = st.text_input("Please input text", key="real_example_callback_reference")

        st.form_submit_button(
            label="Save data", on_click=prepare_insert_database, kwargs=dict(id=0, key_identifier="real_example_callback_reference")
        )

    st.header("Not working solution but the most elegant one (Broken)")

    with st.form(key="real_example_form_not_working", clear_on_submit=True):

        input_reference_2 = st.text_input("Please input text", key="real_example_callback_reference_not_working")

        st.form_submit_button(
            label="Save data", on_click=insert_database, kwargs=dict(id=0, text=st.session_state.real_example_callback_reference_not_working)
        )

    if st.button(label="Clear-Cache"):
        for item in st.session_state:
            del st.session_state[item]


main()

```

**Expected behavior:**

In my opionion, there should be a way to directly forward the values out of the form submission to the callback function. How can we cut the boilerplate code?

**Actual behavior:**

In the example you can see 3 ways. 
1. Using if-button logic to achieve the desired result but we other drawbacks
2. This is a working example with the additional middleware function to retrieve the values from the session state
3. This would be one elegant solution without the need to write boilerplate code.

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no

After calling experimental rerun before a checkbox the session state set by the checkbox is reset to the default value but the checkbox stays in the previous state. Any other cause to rerun the  script such as deactivating and reactivating the checkbox restores the correct state.

### Steps to reproduce

```

if st.button("Experimental rerun"):
```

title: Streamlit-sortables bugs out when adding new items to it during runtime.
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

I am attempting to use streamlit-sortables to create text processing pipelines (a set of interoperable functions). What we do is allow the user to create an operation. This operation is added to the pipeline. However, perhaps a user wishes to change the order that operations run, streamlit-sortables works well for this. 

However we are running into when we try to add new items to these lists (via some button press). 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit_sortables import sort_items

if not "pipeline_left" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.pipeline_left = ['item1', 'item2', 'item3']

if not "pipeline_right" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.pipeline_right = ['item4', 'item5', 'item6']

button = st.button("ADD", key="BUTTON")

if button:
    st.session_state.pipeline_left.append("ADDED")

items = [
    {'header': 'Pipeline', 'items': st.session_state.pipeline_left},
    {'header': 'Disabled', 'items': st.session_state.pipeline_right},
]

sorted_items = sort_items(items, multi_containers=True, direction='vertical')
```


### Steps To Reproduce

I.E Streamlit starts up. You initialize the streamlit sortable via the following:

```
items = [
    {'header': 'Pipeline', 'items': ["item1","item2,","item3"]},
    {'header': 'Disabled', 'items': ["item4","item5,","item6"]},
]


sorted_items = sort_items(items, multi_containers=True, direction='vertical')
```

All is well. Items can be moved between lists and reordered as per usual. But we wish for the end-user to be able to assemble a pipeline themselves. Meaning they need to be able to add new elements to the lists. 

We thought we'd implement that using session state:
```
if not "pipeline_left" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.pipeline_left = ['item1', 'item2', 'item3']

if not "pipeline_right" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.pipeline_right = ['item4', 'item5', 'item6']

button = st.button("ADD", key="BUTTON")

if button:
    st.session_state.pipeline_left.append("ADDED")

items = [
    {'header': 'Pipeline', 'items': st.session_state.pipeline_left},
    {'header': 'Disabled', 'items': st.session_state.pipeline_right},
]

sorted_items = sort_items(items, multi_containers=True, direction='vertical')
```

As you can see, when a button element is clicked, the item "ADDED" is added to the pipeline_left list which is stored in session_state. This means that on reload, the sorted_items element should be populated with the new items. This proceeds as expected. 

The issue occurs when you then try to reorder the sortable list via the frontend. Something is going wrong that is preventing the sortable list for updating correctly and it becomes unresponsive (i) forgets the added element entirely (ii) if you drag ADD from pipeline_left to pipeline_right, when a new element is added, all previously added items appear in pipeline_left. Ignoring all previous state changes. 


### Expected Behavior

We expect to be able to add new elements to the sortable_items list during runtime without completely breaking it's functionality

### Current Behavior

becomes unresponsive (i) 
forgets the added element entirely (ii) 
if you drag "ADDED" from pipeline_left to pipeline_right, when a new element is added (via a second button press), all previously added items appear in pipeline_left. Ignoring all previous state changes. 

Something in streamlit_sortables is not talking to the streamlit backend correctly. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Operating System:
- Browser:
- Virtual environment:

title: Data placed in session_state is lost when debugging outside of Streamlit run
body:
### Problem
I'm not sure if this is a feature request or a regression as this behaviour did work in previous releases.

Whenever I get into more complex problems with a Streamlit app I was able to run the code in a debugger, now I run into the issue that values stored into the session_state are lost, as it appears that the session_state is reconstructed cleanly every time it is accessed.

To get around this, I have to add the following code to my app:

``` python
# When debugging locally, the session state is reconstructed with every request
st.session_state['test'] = 'present'
if 'test' not in st.session_state:
    logger.warning('Session state being replaced in debugger')
    # Replace with a simple dict for the duration of this debugging run
    st.session_state = {}
else:
    del st.session_state['test']
```

### Solution
The simplest solution is to treat code running outside of `streamlit run` as still being in a session, granted it is not associated with an HTTP session, but is still in a session for the duration of the run.

I'm more than happy for the above code to be integrated into the codebase if it helps.  Maybe with the warning message being updated to indicate that session_state is being replaced with a dict for the duration of the run outside of `streamlit run`.

### Additional context
The issue can be reproduced with this code:

```python
import streamlit as st
print(f'Version: {st.__version__}')
st.session_state['test'] = 'present'
print('Keys:')
for k, v in st.session_state.items():
    print(f'{k} = {v}')
print('Done')
```

Which produces the following output, which you will note does not display the information added to the session_state, but does raise a warning:

```
C:\Projects\example\venv\Scripts\python.exe C:/Users/etc/scratches/scratch_19.py
Version: 1.11.1
Keys:
Done
2022-10-28 10:29:56.602 WARNING streamlit.state.session_state_proxy: Session state does not function when running a script without `streamlit run`
Process finished with exit code 0
```
